title: Prefill Velocity Shaper and Attention Hinting for Tail-Latency Mitigation
creator: Anika Shah
description:
Problem: Continuous-batching admission spikes and sudden prefill bursts create long tail latencies for short interactive requests. Existing admission heuristics reduce average latency but still exhibit 95th/99th percentile spikes when microbursts or heterogeneous sequence-length mixes arrive.

Goal: Implement a runtime-side admission and shaping layer (Prefill Velocity Shaper) that smooths prefill inflow at the slot/queue boundary while exposing lightweight attention hints from the model loader so the kernel selector can warm/choose specialized attention kernels ahead of decode. Deliver measurable improvements to tail latency (95th/99th) with minimal throughput regression.

Scope: Engineering work touches admission controller, prefill scheduler, kernel selection path, and small model-loading hooks for attention hint metadata. No model-retraining is required — hints are metadata and optional. For Dedicated/Private we will gate the feature behind feature flags and per-tenant tuning profiles.
acceptance_criteria: 95th-token latency reduced by >=20% for mixed short+long workload in lab replay compared to baseline
99th-token latency reduced by >=15% for same workload
Aggregate throughput loss <= 2% at steady state under typical traffic profiles
No functional regressions in decoding (all existing unit/integration tests pass)
Feature gated and tunable via runtime config with sensible defaults
progress_updates: 2026-02-12: Scoping and design kickoff. Collected traces from runtime persecutor and prefix-KV heatmaps (ref: drive/confluence link). Identified three common microburst patterns: short-batched spiky, long-prefill floods, and mixed-tenanted bursts.

2026-02-15: Prototype for velocity shaper implemented in admission layer (local branch). Uses a leaky-bucket token budget per-slot with dynamic decay constant tuned from 7 days of production traces. Initial sim reduces synthetic tail by 18% but increases mean token wait by ~0.8ms.

2026-02-18: Added attention hint metadata to model manifest loader (optional key: attention_profile: { "preferred_kernel": "kv-sparse", "prefetch_window": "16" }). Runtime reads hint and records kernel warmup score. Implemented early-kernel-probe path: when a prefill stream matches hint conditions we issue a short warmup decode probe to populate kernels/KV cache.

2026-02-21: Bench run with mixed workload replay (short 8-token chat + long 1024 token completions). Observed 95th latency reduction 23% in lab (baseline runtime-1.22) and 1.5% throughput regression under high sustained load. Dashboard: perf/gpu-prefill-vel-shaper-2026-02-21.

2026-02-25: Design review with PM and SRE. Agreed to add per-tenant conservative defaults and an opt-in aggressive mode. Raised concern about potential cost increase due to extra kernel probes; agreed to cap probe frequency and piggy-back probes during low-util periods.

2026-02-27: Open PRs for admission changes and model manifest support. Running canary on internal staging with traffic shadowing. Observed two regressions in decode ordering under corner case (small-slot eviction race) — mitigation implemented to linearize slot state updates (PR linked).
2026-02-28: Stability pass and extended replay shows 95th improvement holds across three different tenant mixes. Preparing release notes and rollout plan for runtime-1.24 canary.
decisions: Use a per-slot leaky-bucket token budget as primary shaping primitive rather than hard queue depth caps (less invasive to throughput).
Keep attention hints optional and backward compatible; runtime falls back to existing kernel heuristics when hints absent.
Limit early-kernel-probe to 'probe budget' per GPU to bound additional compute cost; probe scheduling favors low-util windows.
Expose two runtime modes: conservative (default) and aggressive (opt-in) with clear cost/latency trade-offs in Console.
Rollout behind a feature flag and a per-tenant profile to allow staged tuning for Dedicated customers.
tradeoffs_and_risks: Kernel probes warm caches but cost cycles; aggressive mode may increase tail-work and cost per token — we cap probes to mitigate.
Shaping reduces tail latencies at the cost of small mean token wait; customer-visible latency could increase for some non-critical background jobs — mitigated via tenant profiles.

Attention hints require model manifest changes; though optional, inconsistent or incorrect hints could steer runtime to suboptimal kernels. We will provide tooling to validate hints via offline benchmarks.
Edge-case race observed in slot eviction when probe and prefill complete concurrently — fixed by ordering update + CAS retry, added deterministic test in CI.
tests_and_metrics: Added replay harness scenario: mixed-short-long-8x workload (script: tests/replays/mixed_short_long_8x.yaml)
New SLO smoke test: 95th token latency under 120ms for interactivity profile; CI job added runtime/ci/95th-smoke
Telemetry events: admission.shaper.event, attention.hint.apply, kernel.probe. Each event includes slot_id, tenant_id, chosen_kernel, and probe_outcome
next_steps: Staging canary (Feb 28 - Mar 4): shadow real traffic and enable conservative mode for 10% of hosts
Add automated cost-estimation in Console for aggressive mode (Mar 3)
Run extended replay for 30 days of traces to validate tail behavior across business cycles (Mar 6)
Prepare rollout playbook and feature flag toggle with emergency rollback plan (Mar 8)
Post-release: collect customer feedback and iterate on hint validation tooling
release_notes: Adds Prefill Velocity Shaper (conservative default) and optional Attention Hinting metadata to reduce tail latencies for mixed-length workloads. Feature gated and available in runtime-1.24.
